response.sql:
WITH total_records AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total FROM player_college
),
matched_records AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(c.state, '') as state,
    COUNT(*) as count_matched
  FROM player_college pc
  INNER JOIN college c ON pc.college_id = c.college_id
  GROUP BY COALESCE(c.state, '')
)
SELECT 
  mr.state,
  mr.count_matched,
  CAST(mr.count_matched AS NUMERIC) / CAST(tr.total AS NUMERIC) as ratio
FROM matched_records mr
CROSS JOIN total_records tr
ORDER BY mr.state;

assumptions.assumption: "Blank or missing state is its own group" means NULL and empty-string state values should be grouped together using COALESCE; the output state for this group will be an empty string.

alternatives.interpretation: If blank and missing should be treated as two separate groups (interpreting the phrase as "blank state OR missing state, each their own group"), GROUP BY c.state directly without COALESCE, which keeps NULL and empty string as distinct groups.
